source_document: US Dam Hazard Classification — Corrected Edition (Nov 9, 2026, Nicholas Bendickson), Appendix A — Methods catalog for plugin hazard screening
disclaimer: Informational screening aid, not legal or engineering advice and not a regulatory determination. The output is a suggested classification; the engineer of record and the regulating agency make the determination. Rules change: the current statutes, rules and agency guidance control. Items marked (unverified) or (secondary) should be confirmed before a preset is relied on, and every suggestion still needs an engineer's review.

verification_legend.verified: Confirmed against a primary or official source in the source document (unmarked statements).
verification_legend.secondary: Only a secondary source was found (source document label: Secondary).
verification_legend.unverified: Not confirmed; carried for reference only (source document label: Unverified).
verification_legend.draft: The governing guidance is itself marked DRAFT.

general.base_class_note: With no hit the suggestion is the lowest consequence class (Low). Minimal / Very Low / No Public Hazard need an engineer's call (no method returns ordinal 0).
general.wet_min_depth_note: Plugin default: any depth above this counts as inundated (Appendix A: 'inundated at any depth').
general.sampling_note: Sampling defaults copied from DamSafety_Hazard (constants.OSM_EDGE_BUFFER_FT = 5 ft edge ring around an outline, DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS_FT = 20 ft disc around a point, LINE_SAMPLE_STEP_FT = 10 ft along roads and rail). Not from the source document; editable.

S1.name: Sunny-day failure at normal pool
S1.condition: Sunny-day failure at normal pool (lowest ungated spillway crest or typical operating level).
S1.source: Appendix A.2; common baseline, named explicitly by New York and Virginia.

S2.name: Sunny-day failure, reservoir full to the high water line
S2.condition: Sunny-day failure with the reservoir full to the high water line (emergency spillway crest, or dam crest if none).
S2.source: Appendix A.2; Colorado 2 CCR 402-1 Rules 4.13-4.14; Rhode Island uses water at the top of the embankment for new and currently-Low dams.

S3.name: Water at top of dam or PMF peak, whichever is lower
S3.condition: Water at the top of dam or the PMF peak, whichever is lower; no added inflow; no coincident downstream flooding.

S4.name: Peak pool of the 100-year flood routing
S4.condition: Peak pool during routing of the 100-year flood, never below the auxiliary spillway crest; no coincident downstream flooding.

S5.name: Flood plus failure (rainy day), incremental
S5.condition: SDF or PMF with failure versus the same flood without failure; count only the incremental rise.
S5.source: Appendix A.2; New York (rainy-day run); Virginia 4VAC50-20-54 E requires SDF with and without failure and PMF with failure.

S6.name: Scenario set by the dam's current class
S6.condition: New or Low → S2 at top of embankment; existing High → ½ PMF; existing Significant → 500-year storm.

S7.name: Multiple breach locations
S7.condition: Multiple breach locations along an above-grade impoundment; most severe governs.

D1.name: Incremental-rise cutoff
D1.rule: Routing may stop where the incremental rise falls to about 2 ft or less (a judgment point, not absolute).

D2.name: Convergence cutoff
D2.rule: Routing may stop where breach and non-breach water surfaces converge within 1 ft.

M1.name: Depth–velocity lethality charts
M1.rule: A point in the high-danger zone → High; in the judgment zone → flagged for engineer review; in the low-danger zone → not lethal (passes to M6).

params.chart_for_type_note: Which chart applies to which receptor type is a plugin default (TM-11 names the charts: houses on foundations, mobile homes, passenger vehicles, adults, children); edit it per study.

M1.source: USBR ACER TM-11 (1988) Figures 2–6; North Dakota REG_05.2026 Figs 5.1–5.2 (two charts, 2D model required); New York TOGS 3.1.5 (above Low Danger at the lowest occupied floor → Class C).

M2.name: Flat depth threshold at habitable structures
M2.rule: Depth above the threshold at one or more structures → High.
M2.source: North Dakota REG_05.2026 § 5 (greater than 2 ft, 1D models only); Idaho IDAPA 37.03.06 / IDWR (2 ft or more at residences is sufficient, not the only reason, for High).

M3.name: Structure-type depth and DV matrix
M3.rule: Assign the class from the matrix.

params.rows_note: High at high_depth_ft or more at the datum, or DV high_dv or more; otherwise Low below low_below_ft (a low_below_ft of 0 means at or below the datum: below the foundation ground line), else Significant; Unoccupied farm or storage buildings: Low when flow is above the foundation line. Walkout basements may use walkout_high_depth_ft in place of the home row's high depth where occupants can move upstairs (walkout_option).

M3.source: Nebraska NeDNR/DWEE Classification of Dams (December 2023) Table 3.

M4a.name: Structure count by depth
M4a.rule: N or more occupied structures with depth of X or more → High.
M4a.source: Nebraska Classification of Dams (Dec. 2023): 20 or more occupied structures flooded 2 ft or more above foundation ground line ('should').

M4b.name: Homes count × depth table
M4b.rule: Class from the homes-count × depth table; the worst cell governs.
M4b.source: New York 6 NYCRR 673.5(b) and DOW TOGS 3.1.5 (still marked DRAFT): homes flooded by depth at lowest occupied floor.

M4c.name: Lives or habitable structures in the inundation area
M4c.rule: 1–6 lives or 1–2 habitable structures → Significant; 7 or more lives or 3 or more habitable structures → High.

M5.name: Lives-in-jeopardy count
inputs: people at risk in dangerous depth–velocity zones (from M1 or M2)
M5.rule: Compare the lives-in-jeopardy count with sig_min and high_min.
M5.source: FEMA 333 (probable loss of one or more lives → High); USBR ACER TM-11 (1–6 Significant, more than 6 High); BIA per FEMA P-919 (secondary); Virginia 4VAC50-20-52 (incremental damage analysis, TM-11 Section III, supports lowering a proposed class).

M6.name: Non-lethal flooding of occupied structures
M6.rule: Inundation of a habitable structure at any depth, without lethal conditions → Significant.

variants.any_inundation: Habitable structure inundated at any depth without lethal conditions.
variants.uninhabitable_inoperable: Damage that leaves structures where people live, work or recreate uninhabitable or inoperable (needs a damage_state attribute).
variants.indirect_life_loss: Damage to developed property or infrastructure that may cause indirect loss of life, for example a road washout leading to crashes (needs an indirect_life_loss attribute).

M6.source: North Dakota REG_05.2026 § 5 ('may be classified as medium hazard if there are no other hazards': advisory); Colorado 2 CCR 402-1 (uninhabitable or inoperable); Idaho IDWR (indirect loss of life).

M7.name: Population threshold for a top tier
inputs: critical facilities posing a significant public-safety threat
M7.rule: Expected loss of at least one life and either a population of 1,000 or more in the inundation area, or inundation of critical facilities posing a significant public-safety threat → Extremely High.
M7.source: California 23 CCR § 335.4 (critical facilities: case by case).

M8a.name: Road traffic bands
M8a.rule: Private or AADT under 500 → Low; U.S. or state highway, or AADT 500–2,000 → Significant; interstate or AADT over 2,000 → High. AADT of exactly 500 falls in Significant.

M8b.name: Sole access road
M8b.rule: A road that is the only access to a residence, business or other occupied location → at least Significant.

M8c.name: Road lanes × depth over road
M8c.rule: Interstate or 4+-lane main highway: any flow under the split → Significant, at or above → High. U.S. or state highway under 4 lanes: under the split → Low, at or above → Significant. Other maintained public roads: any flow → Low.

M8d.name: Road functional class
M8d.rule: Principal arterials (interstate, expressway, urban other) → High; urban minor arterial, rural principal arterial other, rural minor arterial, urban collector, rural major collector → Significant; rural minor collector and local roads → Low. Any road with AADT at or under the minor-road limit → Low.
M8d.source: New York TOGS 3.1.5 (DRAFT), NYSDOT functional class.

M8e.name: Low-volume road exclusion
M8e.rule: Roads with AADT at or under the limit may be treated as limited use, so a dam whose only impact is such roads can be Low. AADTs of several limited-use roads are summed unless they carry the same trips.

M8f.name: Isolation of homes
inputs: homes or housing units cut off from emergency services
M8f.rule: Cutting off N or more homes or housing units from emergency services, or failing many road or driveway crossings → Significant.

M8g.name: Road washout examples
M8g.rule: Washout of a state or federal highway, washout of two or more municipal roads, or loss of vehicle access to residences → Significant.

M9a.name: Rail: active line, heavy freight or passenger
M9a.rule: Any impact to an active rail line → at least Significant; freight line with N or more trains per day, or any active passenger line → High.

M9b.name: Rail: main vs minor line by depth
M9b.rule: Main line (N or more trains per day): flow under the split → Significant, at or above → High. Minor line: under the split → Low, at or above → Significant.

M9c.name: Rail: line category
M9c.rule: Intercity passenger, commuter or transit lines, and Class 1 or 2 freight → High; scenic or tourist lines and other freight → Significant; fuel-delivery lines acting as utilities, strategic or defense connectors, and yards or sidings that could release toxic-inhalation hazmat → High.

M10a.name: Critical facilities: isolation and flooding
M10a.rule: Isolation of hospitals, nursing homes, or fire or police stations by floodwater → Significant; flooding a hospital by the depth limit or more → High.

M10b.name: Institutions by depth and DV
inputs: depth at lowest normally occupied level
M10b.source: Appendix A.4 (points to the M3 institutions row, Nebraska Table 3).

M11a.name: Lifelines: reduced effectiveness or blocked access
inputs: lifeline impacted, reduced or access blocked
M11a.rule: Any impact that reduces a lifeline's effectiveness or blocks access to it → at least Significant.

M11b.name: Lifelines: exposure, generation flooding, outage
M11b.rule: Exposed buried lines, or undermined towers and poles → Significant; flow above the first floor of a generation facility, or service interruption longer than the outage limit → High.

M11c.name: Lifelines: important utilities and wastewater plants
M11c.rule: 'Important' utilities serve N or more residential units: interruption of the short-outage limit or less → Significant; loss to major populations or for several weeks → High. Damage to a major or significant-minor wastewater plant → Significant; lesser plant → Low. Loss of the dam's own water-supply reservoir alone does not normally drive the class.

params.high_outage_note: 'Several weeks' is not a number in the source; set high_outage_days per study or mark major_population on the lifeline.

M12a.name: Cultural sites by mitigation
M12a.rule: Damage to major archaeological sites, national monuments or state historic sites: major mitigation needed → Significant; extensive or impossible to mitigate → High.

M12b.name: Substantial environmental damage
inputs: substantial-damage flag or type (long-term loss of listed-species habitat, contaminated sediments)
M12b.rule: Substantial environmental damage, such as long-term loss of listed-species habitat or release of contaminated sediments → Significant.

M12c.name: Important fish waters
M12c.rule: Probable damage to waters identified as important for anadromous fish spawning, rearing or migration → Significant.

M12d.name: Intangible losses identified by a resource agency
M12d.rule: Intangible losses identified by a resource agency, weighed by whether the feature is common or unique and the change temporary or permanent. The source gives no class for this: every such feature is flagged for the engineer.

M13.name: Qualitative descriptor match
inputs: feature presence (descriptor attribute, or receptor type / class)
M13.rule: Fallback when only feature presence is known, not depths. A descriptor set on the receptor is applied as a rule; a descriptor guessed from the receptor's type is advisory and flagged.

params.auto_map_note: auto_map is a plugin default that guesses a descriptor from the receptor type; a home in the general wording is guessed as 'isolated_homes' (Significant), a lower bound: serious damage to homes is High, and an engineer decides.

M13.source: FEMA 333; NRCS NEM Part 520 § 520.21 (wording unverified); New York 6 NYCRR 673.5; Virginia 4VAC50-20-40 wording as a variant.
M13.verification_note: The NRCS definitions' wording is marked (Unverified) in the source document.

R1.name: Transient-use exclusion
R1.rule: People only occasionally or briefly in the inundation area (recreational day users, passers-by, trespassers, non-overnight outdoor users) do not by themselves create probable life loss.

variants.general: Receptors with transient occupancy are left out of the life-safety methods.
variants.incidental: People only incidentally present (walking on the dam, driving lightly traveled roads, recreating outside an established area) are left out.
variants.three_part_test: Loss of life is unlikely only if people are temporary, there are no residences or overnight campsites, and the owner controls access and keeps an EAP with a warning process; otherwise transients are not left out.

R1.source: FEMA 333; New York TOGS 3.1.5; Rhode Island 250-RICR-130-05-1 § 1.5(A)(24); Arizona A.A.C. R12-15-1206(B)(1)(a).

R2.name: Occupancy presumption
R2.rule: Habitable structures, including regularly occupied farm or commercial buildings and overnight recreation, are assumed occupied; occasionally used outbuildings are not. Optionally a home shown flooded is assumed flooded above its lowest occupied floor unless data show otherwise.
R2.source: North Dakota REG_05.2026 § 5; New York TOGS 3.1.5 (floor presumption).

R3.name: No evacuation credit
R3.rule: Emergency action plans and evacuation do not lower the class.

R4.name: Dams in series
R4.rule: Where an upstream failure could cause or contribute to a downstream failure, the upstream class is at least the downstream class.
R4.source: Nebraska Classification of Dams ('must': rule); North Dakota REG_05.2026 § 5.3 and New York ('should': advisory).

R5.name: Future development
R5.source: North Dakota REG_05.2026 § 5.3 (approved plans, permits or active construction); Virginia (locally approved planned land use); Arizona (zoning and development projected over 10 years); NRCS (existing and future development); Texas 30 TAC § 299.14 (existing development).

R6.name: Proximity rule for new dams
R6.rule: A new dam within the listed distance of a municipality of the listed class is designed to High unless downstream development is legally curtailed. Reported as a design requirement; it does not change the consequence class unless raises_class is set.
R6.source: Nebraska Classification of Dams (Dec. 2023) proximity rule.

R7.name: Borderline goes higher
R7.rule: A borderline result takes the higher class. Judgment-zone hits from M1 are always flagged.

params.near_margin_note: The source gives no borderline margin; set near_margin_ft to promote M1 points within that depth below the high-danger line.

R8.name: Simplified-analysis limits
R8.rule: Without a breach model, a class below High can be justified only for dams storing under the storage limit at the top of dam. Approximate methods may confirm Low or Significant, but lowering a dam from High needs TM-11-based unsteady modeling.

variants.storage_limit: No breach model and storage at or over the limit (or unknown): a class below High is not justified → High.
variants.lowering_from_high: Current class High and the analysis is not TM-11-based unsteady modeling: the class is not lowered.

R8.source: North Dakota REG_05.2026 § 5 (storage_limit, 200 ac-ft); New York TOGS 3.1.5 (lowering_from_high).

R9.name: Incremental damage analysis scope
R9.rule: Whether an incremental (S5) result may lower the class found without it.
R9.source: North Dakota REG_05.2026 (may reduce the inflow design flood but never the hazard class); Virginia 4VAC50-20-52 (may lower a proposed class).

R10.name: Re-review trigger
R10.rule: Store the run date and the receptor-layer versions; re-run when downstream layers change.
R10.source: Colorado 2 CCR 402-1 Rule 5.4; Arizona (every inspection); Rhode Island § 1.11(A)(5) (at least every 10 years for Low and Significant dams); New York 673.5(d); MSHA.

USBR.label: USBR (ACER TM-11)
USBR.notes: S5 for borderline dams is (unverified). In this preset M1 marks the lives in jeopardy (high-danger zone) that M5 counts (TM-11: 1–6 Significant, more than 6 High); M1 returns no class by itself (high_class null). TM-11 Figs 4–6 (vehicles, adults, children) are not digitized in this plugin: M1 flags those receptors.

BIA.label: BIA
BIA.notes: BIA's 1–6 Significant rule is from FEMA P-919 (July 2012): (secondary). No scenario confirmed: fall back to M13 and engineering judgment.

NRCS.label: NRCS (NEM Part 520)
NRCS.notes: NRCS hazard-definition wording (NEM § 520.21) is (unverified) in the source document.

ND.label: North Dakota (REG_05.2026)

R5.basis: approved plans, permits or active construction

ND.notes: N.D. Admin. Code § 89-08-01-01; DWR policy REG_05.2026 effective April 1, 2026 (superseded REG_05.2024a). 'Significant' means the same as 'Medium'. The ND Dam Design Handbook was not reviewed.

NE.label: Nebraska (DWEE Classification of Dams, Dec. 2023)
NE.notes: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 46-1601 et seq.; Title 458. Minimal is generally limited to farm pond dams (engineer's call).

NY.label: New York (6 NYCRR 673.5; TOGS 3.1.5 draft)
NY.notes: DOW TOGS 3.1.5 is still marked DRAFT. Class D (defunct dam) is an administrative status and is left out. Sunny-day and rainy-day breaches: the most severe governs.

VA.label: Virginia (4VAC50-20-40, amended Jan 14, 2026)
VA.scenario_note: S5 covers the four 4VAC50-20-54 E analyses: sunny-day, SDF with failure, SDF without failure, PMF with failure.
VA.notes: Significant may cause loss of life. Significant dams of 50,000 ac-ft or more held to the High SDF is (unverified) and not used here. M5 is the incremental-analysis variant: it supports lowering a proposed class only.

ID.label: Idaho (IDAPA 37.03.06 Rule 25)
ID.notes: 2 ft or more at residences is sufficient (not the only reason) for High. Pre-2023 versions used a 2 ft / 2 fps test (not used).

CO.label: Colorado (2 CCR 402-1)
CO.notes: Rule 4.13 sunny-day failure, reservoir full to the high water line (Rule 4.14). The Rule 4.15 Hydrologic Hazard sizes spillways and is not covered.

RI.label: Rhode Island (250-RICR-130-05-1)
RI.notes: Scenario depends on the current class (§ 1.9(B)). The Director evaluates Low and Significant dams at least every 10 years.

AZ.label: Arizona (A.A.C. R12-15-1206)

R5.basis: zoning and development projected over 10 years

AZ.notes: Classification regardless of the dam's condition. Very Low needs an engineer's call.

CA.label: California (23 CCR § 335.4)
CA.scenario_note: Sunny-day loading condition (no S-code is given in Appendix A.6; supply the sunny-day run as S1 or S2).
CA.notes: Extremely High for critical facilities is case by case. DWR's older 'considerable loss of life' wording is superseded by the regulation.
